text:
amelia (support): quick heads up — ACME reported a sharp p95 jump on /v1/generate starting ~10:10 UTC, p95 ~1.2s -> normal ~220ms. customer saw 503s around same time. logs show OOMs on gpu-23. filing here for triage
liam (eng-runtime): thanks. are there recent deploys or routing changes? any KV growth traces? :thinking_face:
amelia (support): no deploys on their dedicated pool, they are on dedicated-nyc-2. their quota is steady. here's a snippet from the tenant logs (trimmed):
```
2026-03-15T10:09:41Z ERROR allocator: OOM: failed alloc 268435456
2026-03-15T10:09:41Z WARN  kvcache: resident_size=67.4GB growth_delta=1.2GB evictions=0
2026-03-15T10:09:42Z INFO  request: id=abc123 route=/v1/generate latency=1180ms status=503
```
priya (eng-sre): kvcache evictions=0 and growth_delta +1.2GB is suspicious — sounds like eviction/oscillation failed. which allocator flags are set on that pool?
liam (eng-runtime): looking now. dedicated-nyc-2 had allocator: `--alloc-mode=dynamic --evict-threshold=0.86 --evict-min-free=2GB` for the node group. that evict-threshold is a bit high for current load.
amelia (support): customer reports they were running a long chat session with many turns, prompt sizes ~1.5k tokens, a lot of pipeline concurrent requests (burst of ~90).
marco (customer): yes, we saw tail errors while running a batch of user-sessions. we can repro with the script below — sends 90 concurrent sessions with multi-turns.
```
for i in `seq 1 90`; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"<~1500 tokens>","max_tokens":256}' &
done
wait
```
priya (eng-sre): good repro. immediate mitigations we can try: 1) lower evict-threshold to 0.7 to force earlier KV eviction 2) enable passive prefix-eviction for large sessions 3) temporarily cap concurrency for this tenant to 40 4) route overflow to a compatible quantized model in the pool with more free memory.
liam (eng-runtime): I'll push a canary change to dedicated-nyc-2 with `--evict-threshold=0.72` and `--kv-passive-evict=true` to the routing slice handling ACME. will monitor p95 and evictions.
ops-bot: deploy queued by liam for pool dedicated-nyc-2/canary (change id ch-8791).
priya (eng-sre): while that rolls, we should gather KV heatmap + per-node resident sizes for last 2 hours. liam can you attach heatmap once canary is up? also capture `malloc_stats` from the allocator on gpu-23.
liam (eng-runtime): +1. collecting heatmap now, will paste when ready. starting canary in 30s.
amelia (support): notifying ACME about temporary concurrency cap and failover route. message: "We're rolling a mitigation to reduce OOM pressure (short-term config change + route fallback). Expect improved p95 within ~5-7min"
marco (customer): thanks. we'll hold non-critical traffic for 15m and run the repro script after you confirm.
(liam posts): heatmap (trimmed) -> node gpu-23: hot_keys=12 large_prefixes=5 kv_bytes=65GB; node gpu-24: kv_bytes=22GB; eviction_count gpu-23=0
priya (eng-sre): confirms eviction not triggering on gpu-23 despite high kv_bytes. allocator fragmentation looks likely — see `malloc_stats` shows many small free slabs but no contiguous region for big allocations.
liam (eng-runtime): canary rolled. quick metrics: within 90s evictions started on gpu-23: evictions=31, kv_bytes dropped to 58GB, p95 down to 310ms. but p99 still at ~1.1s for a few requests.
amelia (support): reporting back to ACME: p95 much improved, p99 tail still healing. asked them to rerun repro in 10m.
marco (customer): reran repro after 12m, p95 stable ~290ms, p99 reduced to 640ms, a few 503s but much better. thanks.
priya (eng-sre): follow-up actions (owner tags):
- liam: backfill telemetry to quantify how often evictions fail on threshold (due 48h)
- liam: propose permanent allocator tuning (lower default evict-threshold + passive-evict enabled) for dedicated pools (PR + canary plan, due 72h)
- ops: add tenant-level concurrency cap feature with auto-trigger on OOM-signal (design doc draft, due 7d)
- support/amelia: update runbook to include quick mitigations list + sample cURL for tenant-side temporary throttling (due 24h)
liam (eng-runtime): I'll open PR with test plan. early note: lowering threshold reduces average latency slightly for small requests but prevents OOM tail events. need perf validation.
amelia (support): closing loop with ACME, will keep thread updated if they regress. :thumbsup:
